 Memphis Grizzlies The Memphis Grizzlies improved to 12-4 with a 126-98 win over the shorthanded Golden State Warriors.
--> The Memphis Grizzlies improved to 12-4 with a 126-98 win over the shorthanded Golden State Warriors.
 Steph Curry and Draymond Green were both out tonight, but that is not to discount the Grizzlies' convincing win on the second night of a back-to-back .
--> Steph Curry and Draymond Green were both out tonight, but that is not to discount the Grizzlies' convincing win on the second night of a back-to-back .
 Here is a look at four winners and one loser from the game.
--> Here is a look at four winners and one loser from the game.
 Winner: Defense 
--> Winner: Defense 
 Memphis' defense set the tone from the beginning of the game, allowing the Grizzlies to grab an early lead and run with it. The Warriors scored just 47 points in the first half and shot 6-for-21 from the field in the second quarter.
--> Memphis' defense set the tone from the beginning of the game, allowing the Grizzlies to grab an early lead and run with it. The Warriors scored just 47 points in the first half and shot 6-for-21 from the field in the second quarter.
 The Grizzlies forced 20 turnovers and scored 35 points off takeaways. That was a big part of a performance that held Golden State to a 17 percent clip from three and under 100 points for the fifth time this season.

— eric (@EricTweetsNBA) November 20, 2026 Winner: Cedric Coward
--> Winner: Cedric Coward
 Coward has arguably been the Grizzlies' best all-around player this season and he continued his strong start with 19 points, four rebounds and four assists on 7-for-14 shooting. He was also a big part of Memphis' solid defensive performance, as he usually is.

 Cedric Coward with 13 points and 3 threes for far in the first half pic.twitter.com/yjsTGF6Nnc 
— eric (@EricTweetsNBA) November 20, 2026 Along with Jaylen Wells, Coward's development as a three-point shooter has been a big deal for a Grizzlies team that thrives on spacing the floor. He came into the game shooting 45.2 percent from outside and went 5-for-9 from three tonight.

 Winner: Cam Boozer
--> Winner: Cam Boozer
 Cam Boozer has started to right the ship on his low shooting efficiency to start the season. He scored 16 points on 6-for-6 shooting. Since going 2-for-14 against the Oklahoma City Thunder on Nov. 6, Boozer is shooting 52.9 percent from the floor and, arguably more importantly, 59.3 percent from inside the arc in the last seven games.

 Cam Boozer fadeaway whew pic.twitter.com/fxGBskHS8I 
— eric (@EricTweetsNBA) November 20, 2026 Winner: Jaylen Wells
--> Winner: Jaylen Wells
 Wells, as mentioned earlier, is in the midst of a three-point shooting leap. He continued to shoot it well from the outside, going 4-for-5 from three. Improving as a creator has usually been what is talked about in terms of Wells' development. However, increasing his three-point percentage from 35 percent to 40 percent might be just as valuable to the Grizzlies.

 Loser: Second chance points
--> Loser: Second chance points
 Golden State winning the second-chance points battle is the only real stain on this game for Memphis. The Warriors grabbed 18 offensive rebounds to 15 for the Grizzlies and outscored Memphis 25-17 on second-chance opportunities.
